prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: square in-use tool-recognition illustration for a custodial-training image library
Input images: Image 1 is the sole anatomy-only reference. Use it only to understand the assembled mechanical relationship of a traditional straight pipe wrench: one movable hook jaw continuous with one threaded shank, one knurled adjustment nut, one fixed heel jaw, and one handle. Generate a new original illustration from scratch; do not edit, trace, restyle, or reproduce the photographed product. Do not borrow Image 1's color, brand, lettering, camera angle, composition, exact contours, proportions, surface details, or trade dress.

Primary request: Create an original monochrome instructional line-art scene showing one generic traditional straight pipe wrench correctly seated on and gripping one round cylindrical metal pipe coupling or round fitting. No person or hand is present. The static working grip should make the tool's intended use clear without arrows or text.

Scene/backdrop: pure white square canvas with no floor, room, bench, border, callout, or decoration.

Subject and contact geometry: Show one thick round steel pipe coupling or fitting as a short, clearly cylindrical object viewed in a simple side-oblique orientation, with a visible curved outer surface and one elliptical circular rim or band that establishes roundness. The fitting must not be hexagonal. Seat the fitting fully inside the wrench's jaw opening. The hook jaw's serrated inner face and the fixed heel jaw's serrated face must oppose each other and touch opposite sides of the fitting tangentially. Both contact points must be visible and plausible: no floating gap, no fused surfaces, and no teeth passing through the fitting. The wrench surrounds only the fitting's outside cylindrical surface.

Wrench mechanism: Depict one movable curved hook jaw continuing into one straight threaded shank on one centerline. That one shank engages exactly one knurled circular adjustment nut seated at the body. Normal housing occlusion is acceptable, but no contradictory second shank, rack, rod, or nut may appear. Depict one fixed heel jaw integral to the body. Show one complete ordinary-length handle with no extension, no cheater bar, and no impact tool.

Style/medium: original black-and-white educational technical line art; crisp graphite-black outer contours, consistent medium interior lines, sparse functional hatching, and restrained pale-gray form wash only where it clarifies the cylinder and tool surfaces; no photographic rendering.

Composition/framing: feature-revealing near-side view with slight depth only to establish the round fitting and jaw contact. The fitting sits left of center, the wrench head encloses it, and the complete handle extends diagonally down toward the right at about 25 degrees. Keep every part of the wrench visible with generous even padding. Make the head, opposed teeth, two contact points, single nut, and cylindrical fitting large and legible after reduction to 320 by 320 pixels.

Constraints: exactly one wrench and one round metal fitting; mechanically plausible connected parts; safe generic use context; original generic contours; pure white background; monochrome only.
Avoid: smooth parallel crescent-wrench jaws; adjustable-wrench worm gear; hex nut or bolt head; square stock; flat plate; duplicated or detached parts; impossible jaw intersection; teeth embedded through metal; loose noncontacting jaws; a second tool or pipe; a person, hand, glove, body, cheater bar, extension pipe, hammer, impact, unsafe pose, workshop scene, color, glossy product photography, cast shadow, logo, brand name, lettering, numerals, labels, arrows, motion marks, dimensions, border, watermark, or copied trade dress.
